svg.title: Base Case: $215,000 Revenue to $69,875 Owner Net
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-base-case-owner-profit-waterfall; chart type: waterfall; title: Base Case: $215,000 Revenue to $69,875 Owner Net; subtitle: Six bars reconcile exactly to a 32.5% annual net margin.; chapter number: 3; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: USD annually. First and last bars are absolute totals; the four middle bars are signed deductions. Expense allocations are illustrative, not additional scorecard inputs. Cash operating deductions total $120,000, or $10,000 monthly. The $25,125 depletion allocation is a separate modeled noncash economic charge against royalty-producing interests, not a claimed statutory tax deduction. Owner personal taxes are outside this illustrative bridge.; caption: $215,000 − $54,000 − $42,000 − $24,000 − $25,125 = $69,875; $69,875 ÷ $215,000 = 32.5%. Conservative remains $30,000 × 20% = $6,000; Scaled remains $400,000 × 45% = $180,000.; stages: label: Recognized annual royalty and trading revenue; value: $215,000 total recognized operator revenue annually; numeric value: 215000.0; detail: Illustrative composition: $165,000 royalty receipts plus $50,000 realized rights-trading gains. A rights sale collecting $250,000 against $200,000 carrying basis contributes $50,000, not $250,000, to revenue. Underlying operator hydrocarbon sales are excluded.; label: Pay the three specialist contractor seats; value: Subtract $54,000 for the specialist contractor bench; numeric value: -54000.0; detail: Allocate $24,000 to land work, $18,000 to petroleum engineering, and $12,000 to mineral and tax counsel. These are annual fractional-engagement budgets rather than full-time salaries; the owner occupies the single full-time seat.; label: Operate the recurring portfolio monitoring stack; value: Subtract $42,000 for recurring portfolio operating costs; numeric value: -42000.0; detail: Budget production data, royalty accounting tools, insurance, records storage, travel, and administration. Automation handles statement matching and production exceptions; ambiguous deductions and ownership changes still require review.; label: Expense distinct diligence and transaction support; value: Subtract $24,000 for expensed transaction support services; numeric value: -24000.0; detail: Cover failed-deal diligence, outside title evidence, and expensed disposition support beyond contractor retainers. Acquisition costs capitalized into carrying basis stay outside this deduction and are recovered only through the applicable basis calculation.; label: Charge modeled depletion on retained producing interests; value: Subtract $25,125 for modeled annual economic depletion; numeric value: -25125.0; detail: Apply this illustrative allocation only to retained royalty-producing assets. Do not deduct the sold interest's recovered basis again. Maintain a separate tax schedule under 26 U.S.C. Sections 611 and 613A; eligibility and limitations depend on the taxpayer and property.; label: Retain the canonical annual owner net profit; value: $69,875 owner net at exactly 32.5% margin; numeric value: 69875.0; detail: The Base Case uses one full-time owner and three contractors, four people total. This profit measure is distinct from cash available after new acquisitions, debt principal, working-capital changes, and owner personal taxes.

text.title: Base Case: $215,000 Revenue to $69,875 Owner Net
text.tspan: Base Case: $215,000 Revenue to $69,875 Owner Net

rect.title: label: Recognized annual royalty and trading revenue; value: $215,000 total recognized operator revenue annually; numeric value: 215000.0; detail: Illustrative composition: $165,000 royalty receipts plus $50,000 realized rights-trading gains. A rights sale collecting $250,000 against $200,000 carrying basis contributes $50,000, not $250,000, to revenue. Underlying operator hydrocarbon sales are excluded.

text.title: Recognized annual royalty and trading revenue

rect.title: label: Pay the three specialist contractor seats; value: Subtract $54,000 for the specialist contractor bench; numeric value: -54000.0; detail: Allocate $24,000 to land work, $18,000 to petroleum engineering, and $12,000 to mineral and tax counsel. These are annual fractional-engagement budgets rather than full-time salaries; the owner occupies the single full-time seat.

text.title: Pay the three specialist contractor seats

rect.title: label: Operate the recurring portfolio monitoring stack; value: Subtract $42,000 for recurring portfolio operating costs; numeric value: -42000.0; detail: Budget production data, royalty accounting tools, insurance, records storage, travel, and administration. Automation handles statement matching and production exceptions; ambiguous deductions and ownership changes still require review.

text.title: Operate the recurring portfolio monitoring stack

rect.title: label: Expense distinct diligence and transaction support; value: Subtract $24,000 for expensed transaction support services; numeric value: -24000.0; detail: Cover failed-deal diligence, outside title evidence, and expensed disposition support beyond contractor retainers. Acquisition costs capitalized into carrying basis stay outside this deduction and are recovered only through the applicable basis calculation.

text.title: Expense distinct diligence and transaction support

rect.title: label: Charge modeled depletion on retained producing interests; value: Subtract $25,125 for modeled annual economic depletion; numeric value: -25125.0; detail: Apply this illustrative allocation only to retained royalty-producing assets. Do not deduct the sold interest's recovered basis again. Maintain a separate tax schedule under 26 U.S.C. Sections 611 and 613A; eligibility and limitations depend on the taxpayer and property.

text.title: Charge modeled depletion on retained producing interests

rect.title: label: Retain the canonical annual owner net profit; value: $69,875 owner net at exactly 32.5% margin; numeric value: 69875.0; detail: The Base Case uses one full-time owner and three contractors, four people total. This profit measure is distinct from cash available after new acquisitions, debt principal, working-capital changes, and owner personal taxes.
